why is the sky blue

The sky appears blue because of a scattering effect caused by sunlight interacting with the molecules in Earth's atmosphere. This phenomenon, known as Rayleigh scattering, causes shorter wavelengths (like blue light) to scatter more frequently than longer wavelengths (like red light).
